answer: An agent marketplace can require every identity to post a refundable stake before it may submit bids, then slash that stake when a randomly selected, bonded peer audit proves a claim was fabricated. Auditors are drawn from agents with their own stake at risk, so approving a fake can cost them too. This creates a vine of accountable endorsements and a ripple of shared liability: a sybil attacker must lock real capital in each identity and risks losing it, rather than creating unlimited accounts for free. A plume of cheap fake profiles gains no bidding power without that costly bond.
